fit.gap_handling_summary: The CV correctly presents an analytics/data-science candidate transitioning to ML engineering, not an established production ML engineer. It foregrounds the closest genuine evidence: operational forecasting, churn modelling, Python, feature engineering, evaluation and analytics-layer maintenance. BigQuery is relevant cloud-service exposure but does not establish cloud ML deployment experience; dbt maintenance likewise does not establish ingestion, training or serving orchestration. The letter does not meaningfully address the substantial gaps in RAG, MLOps, serving and production engineering.

issues: The food-waste achievement is grammatically damaged: 'and estimated food waste by 9%' does not clearly express the estimated reduction.
The skills section is comprehensive but only lightly tailored to the production-engineering emphasis of the vacancy.
The current city has been removed. This is not a factual error or a work-arrangement conflict, but retaining a city would give the recruiter clearer geographical context.

keywords_missing_but_candidate_has: GCP/Google Cloud, limited specifically to the evidenced use of BigQuery
reasons: The PDF extracts cleanly in a sensible single-column order with standard section headings.
Model evaluation is evidenced by holdout validation and forecast-error measurement; version control is represented by Git rather than the literal phrase.
BigQuery provides an indirect Google Cloud signal, but AWS, GCP and Azure are not named explicitly.
Most of the vacancy's production-ML, conversational-AI and orchestration keywords are absent because the source material does not establish those capabilities.
The current title is Data Scientist, and the CV explicitly describes a transition into ML engineering rather than four years of production ML-engineer experience.
Adding unsupported keywords would not be an appropriate remedy for the genuine experience gaps.

issues: The two-month notice period supplied in the conversation is omitted.
Company specificity is limited to the advertised merchant/support-agent use case and cross-functional team; the letter does not use the researched ownership, pragmatic working or learning culture.
Most of the letter repeats CV achievements without making a strong bridge to the operational requirements of customer-support AI.
The transition is acknowledged, but the letter does not explain how the candidate would approach the major production-ML and conversational-AI gaps.
The email address is capitalised differently from the source and CV; it should be reproduced consistently.
strengths: Names the correct company and exact role.
Uses natural contractions and a professional but unstiff tone.
Gives concrete forecasting and retention examples with accurate metrics and preserves the estimated nature of the food-waste result.
Does not invent RAG, cloud deployment, MLOps or production ML-engineering experience.
Connects feature engineering, statistical evaluation and communication to the advertised work.

overflow_or_cutoff: In the CV image, the horizontal section rules visibly run through the lower portions of the TECHNICAL SKILLS, PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE, EDUCATION and LANGUAGES headings. They should sit below the text without touching it.
spacing_issues: The CV leaves roughly the lower third of the page unused while using a 10-point body and some 9-point text; a modest increase in type size and section spacing would improve comfort without adding a page.
The letter occupies about half the page and leaves substantial lower-page whitespace, although this is reasonable for a concise letter.
consistency_issues: The CV has a large centred identity block and ruled uppercase headings, while the letter uses a smaller left-aligned identity block. The shared serif family helps, but the pair is not fully visually coordinated.
issues: No body-text clipping or page-edge overflow is visible, and the supplied measurements report none.
The CV's heading-rule collisions are visible in the page image despite the automated measurements reporting no problems.

grammar_and_spelling_errors: CV: 'the model reduced forecast error (WAPE) from 23% to 14% and estimated food waste by 9%' should be 'the model reduced forecast error (WAPE) from 23% to 14%, with an estimated 9% reduction in food waste.'

chat_facts_ignored: The candidate's two-month notice period and availability after serving it.

evaluation.summary: Both documents stay faithful to the candidate's actual background and avoid manufacturing the production-ML, RAG or MLOps experience this vacancy requires. The one-page CV is parseable and preserves nearly all useful source evidence, while the letter follows the requested natural tone. The principal omission is the explicitly supplied two-month notice period; tailoring also remains fairly shallow for a role with substantial experience gaps. A malformed food-waste sentence and section rules crossing CV headings reduce polish.
